name_story.story: Raju can be understood through the Sanskrit form رَاجُو, whose central sense is raju; little king (south asian). Raju is a South Asian male given name, a diminutive from Sanskrit राज (rāja, 'king').

faq.a: Raju is associated with the Sanskrit form رَاجُو, whose core sense is raju; little king (south asian).

faq.q: What is the origin of Raju?
faq.a: Raju is associated with Sanskrit. Raju is a South Asian male given name, a diminutive from Sanskrit राज (rāja, 'king').
No — the underlying form is Sanskrit, not Arabic.
Raju can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Sanskrit-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Raju should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Raju is a Sanskrit-derived name, not a Quranic Arabic form.

faq.q: What does Raju mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Raju is rendered راجو and carries the sense راجو، چھوٹا راجہ.

faq.q: What does Raju mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Raju is rendered راجو and carries the sense راجو، شاهزاده.
A romanized syllable approximation is ra-ju. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Raju?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Raju, raju. Script forms are راجو, رَاجُو, राजू.

faq.q: Is Raju a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
